BLOCK 1 — 0:00–0:15 — THE STORM

@Image1 = Old fisherman, 70s, white stubble, yellow oilskin jacket, navy wool cap
@Image2 = Deck of a small wooden trawler at night in a storm, single sodium deck lamp
@Image3 = Wet stone harbour at dawn, overcast, empty moorings

In each character sheet, take the face from the LEFT chest-up portrait panel. The centre panel omits the head deliberately. The fisherman has a head and face in every shot of this film.

Continuous scene. No dialogue. Heavy rain, gale, sea spray, water beading on the lens. Night. The sodium deck lamp is the only key.
The bandage is on his LEFT hand. The rope coils over his RIGHT shoulder.

0–5s: Handheld wide shot, 24mm anamorphic, low on the deck at knee height, lurching with the swell. @Image1 hauls a dripping net over the gunwale hand over hand, rain driving sideways through the deck lamp's orange cone. Match @Image2's sodium lamp and black sea exactly.
Audio: wind roar, rain hammering the wheelhouse roof, the net slapping wet wood at 3s.

5–8s: Cut. Insert, 50mm, close on the net. A green glass bottle is tangled in the mesh, a rolled paper visible inside, catching the lamp light.
Audio: glass knocking against the deck boards twice.

8–11s: Cut. Close-up, 85mm, static against the motion. @Image1 stops hauling. His eyes fix on the bottle; rain runs off the cap's brim. He does not blink for the full three seconds.
Audio: the wind drops under a single low creak of the hull.

11–15s: Cut. Medium shot, 35mm, handheld. @Image1 frees the bottle with his RIGHT hand and pushes it inside his oilskin jacket, then holds his palm flat over it.
Audio: wind returns, rain, his breath through the nose.

END ON THIS FRAME — @Image1 at frame centre, RIGHT palm flat on his chest over the hidden bottle, deck lamp behind him camera-LEFT.

NEGATIVE: no slow motion, no other people, no text, no CGI water, no calm sea.

Style DNA:
Shot on ARRI Alexa 35 with anamorphic prime lenses. Handheld with subtle micro-shake unless a shot specifies locked-off. Photoreal live-action cinematography, no stylisation. Cold blue-grey ambience, deep crushed blacks, desaturated teal-green palette, skin weathered and natural. 24fps, 180-degree shutter, fine 35mm grain, shallow depth of field. Bleak, lonely, stubborn.

BLOCK 2 — 0:15–0:30 — THE CABIN

@Image1 = Old fisherman
@Image2 = Trawler deck at night
@Image4 = final frame of Block 1

Continuous scene. No dialogue. Storm outside, rain on the roof. Night. A single bare bulb over the chart table is the only key.
The bandage is on his LEFT hand. This clip picks up seconds after the previous one. Continue from @Image4 exactly.

0–4s: Locked-off wide, 24mm, from the corner of the tiny wheelhouse cabin. @Image1 shoulders the door shut against the wind and leans his back on it.
Audio: door thud at 1s, the storm muffles instantly.

4–9s: Cut. Medium close-up, 50mm, slow push-in over the full five seconds. @Image1 draws the bottle out, works the cork with his teeth, spits it aside, and shakes the paper loose onto the chart table.
Audio: cork squeak, a soft pop, paper rustle.

9–15s: Cut. Insert overhead, 50mm. His LEFT hand, bandaged, flattens the paper. Faded pencil handwriting, no legible words, and a child's drawing of a boat. His thumb stops on the drawing and stays there.
Audio: the hull creaking, rain on the roof, nothing else.

END ON THIS FRAME — overhead on the paper, his LEFT thumb resting on the drawing.

NEGATIVE: no legible text on the paper, no slow motion, no other people, no CGI.

@Image1 = Old fisherman

Next morning, new scene. No dialogue. Rain stopped, wet surfaces, flat overcast dawn light.

0–6s: Extreme wide, 24mm, locked-off from the harbour wall. @Image1 walks the length of the empty quay toward camera, small in frame, gulls on the moorings. Match @Image3's flat overcast dawn exactly.

6–10s: Cut. Medium shot, 35mm. @Image1 stops at the end of the quay, takes the paper from his LEFT breast pocket, and unfolds it against the wind.

10–15s: Cut. Wide, 32mm anamorphic, from behind him. @Image1 stands holding the drawing up against the horizon, where a small red boat sits far out on the grey water. He holds it there for the full five seconds and does not lower his arm.
Audio: the gulls go quiet; water against stone; a distant boat horn at 13s.
